name: Acute Patellar Dislocation - First Episode
definition: Acute lateral displacement of the patella from the trochlea, usually after twisting or direct trauma, with risk of osteochondral injury.

typical: Sudden knee deformity or spontaneous reduction

investigations.principle: Radiographs are first-line; MRI is used when osteochondral injury or major soft-tissue damage is suspected.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Surgery is selective after first episode, especially with large osteochondral injury or major instability risk factors.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Janu-Sandhi displacement phenotype may be documented after modern reduction.

patientEducation.summary: Acute lateral displacement of the patella from the trochlea, usually after twisting or direct trauma, with risk of osteochondral injury.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected serious infection, sepsis, pathological instability or other listed red flags.
